### Appendix 2: Additional Analysis {#sec-additional-analysis}
 
#### Mechanical seat-share gains by exact party vote share

@fig-party-size-gains-continuous supplements the @fig-party-size-gains in the Analysis of Hypothesis 1. Conversely to @fig-party-size-gains it uses no grouping and plots each party-election observation at its exact vote share. It shows substantial variation in mechanical seat-share gains among parties with similar vote shares as well as no clear monotonic relationship. Additionally to @fig-party-size-gains it shows that lists with very low vote shares cluster around zero.  @fig-party-size-gains-continuous therefore provides additional context for the group averages reported in the main analysis. As in the grouped figure, grey open circles show Graubünden's hypothetical HB comparison for context only and the observations do not enter the transition summaries.

```{r}
#| label: fig-party-size-gains-continuous
#| fig-cap: "Mechanical seat-share gains by exact party vote share"
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| echo: false
#| message: false

ggplot(party_size_plot_data, aes(x = vote_share, y = gain_pp)) + # Include GR for context at exact vote shares.
  annotate( # add a grey area for groups outside of 10% quroum
    "rect", xmin = 10, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "#F2F2F2"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 10,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, # Mark no difference between DP and HB.
    colour = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = comparison, shape = comparison),
    alpha = 0.6, # Transparency to show overlapping observations
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 15, by = 2.5) # Show ticks and gridlines every 2.5 percentage points.
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Transition cantons" = "#0072B2", "Graubünden (context)" = "#707070"),
    breaks = c("Transition cantons", "Graubünden (context)"), name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Transition cantons" = 16, "Graubünden (context)" = 1),
    breaks = c("Transition cantons", "Graubünden (context)"), name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Party vote share in the analyzed area (%)",
    y = "Seat-share gain under DP relative to HB (pp)",
    caption = wrap_plot_caption(
      "Each point represents one party-election observation below 15% vote share.\n",
      "Grey shading: vote shares at or above 10%, outside the smaller-party definition.\n",
      "Grey open circles: Graubünden's hypothetical HB comparison (context only).",
      width = 100
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11, lineheight = 1.1,
                                margin = margin(t = 8))
  )
```

### Appendix 3:  Leave-one-canton-out robustness checks {#sec-leave-one-out}

The leave-one-canton-out check, is a sensitivity and robustness check, where the statistical results of the thesis are recalculated after the omission of each single canton. Through that it can be observed, whether the results are sensitive to the inclusion of a specific canton or not. The bold values in the following tables, identify the canton omission that produces the largest absolute change from the full-sample result in each outcome column. For EQ3, this comparison is made separately within each election number. The comparisons use unrounded results. 

```{r}
#| label: loco-highlight-helper
#| echo: false

# Return a table-ready copy with the most influential omission in bold
loco_highlight_influence <- function(data, measures, groups = character()) {
  highlight_group <- function(group_data) {
    # Each table or group needs exactly one baseline row for comparison.
    reference_row <- which(group_data$omitted_canton == "Full sample")
    stopifnot(length(reference_row) == 1L)

    for (measure in measures) {
      values <- group_data[[measure]]
      # relevant is absolute distance from baseline 
      deviation <- abs(values - values[reference_row])
      # Exclude the baseline and NA
      candidates <- which(
        group_data$omitted_canton != "Full sample" & is.finite(deviation)
      )
      # Leave column unhighlighted if no valid omission changes result
      strongest <- integer()
      if (length(candidates) > 0L) {
        largest_change <- max(deviation[candidates])
        if (largest_change > 0) {
          # Keep all ties 
          strongest <- candidates[near(deviation[candidates], largest_change)]
        }
      }

      # Only returned copy becomes text
      formatted <- ifelse(is.na(values), "NA", sprintf("%.2f", values))
      formatted[strongest] <- paste0("**", formatted[strongest], "**")
      group_data[[measure]] <- formatted
    }
    group_data
  }

  if (length(groups) == 0L) {
    
    highlight_group(data)
  } else {
    # EQ3: repeat independently per election number
    data |>
      group_by(across(all_of(groups))) |>
      group_modify(~ highlight_group(.x)) |>
      ungroup()
  }
}
```

#### Hypothesis 1 

```{r}
#| label: loco-results-h1
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: [24,24,24,28]

loco_data_h1 <- small_party_summary |>
  filter(!is_graubuenden) |> # Exclude the context-only canton.
  mutate(canton = str_sub(election_id, 1, 2)) # Extract canton codes.

stopifnot(
  nrow(loco_data_h1) == 31L, # Check election count.
  n_distinct(loco_data_h1$canton) == 8L # Check canton count.
)

loco_results_h1 <- map_dfr( # Include the full-sample reference, then omit each canton.
  c("Full sample", sort(unique(loco_data_h1$canton))),
  function(omitted) {

    loco_data_h1 |>
      filter(omitted == "Full sample" | canton != omitted) |>
      summarise(
        omitted_canton = omitted,
        elections = n(), # Count remaining elections.
        mean_gain = mean(seat_gain_pp), # Give each election equal weight.
        weighted_mean_gain = weighted.mean(
          seat_gain_pp, seats_allocated_dp # Weight by analyzed seats.
        )
      )
  }
)

knitr::kable( # Display the results in the appendix.
  loco_highlight_influence(loco_results_h1, c("mean_gain", "weighted_mean_gain")),
  format = "pipe",
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Canton omitted", "Elections remaining",
    "Mean gain (pp)", "Weighted mean gain (pp)"
  ),
  caption = "Smaller-party seat-share gains in the full sample and after excluding each canton."
)
```

Both the unweighted and weighted mean gains are relatively consistent after the exclusion of every canton. The means are sensitive to the omission of Schaffhausen and Zurich for the unweighted respectively the weighted mean. In both cases the gain declines when they are excluded. This is aligned with the observation, that both Zurich and Schaffhausen receive relatively high seat-share gains. Further both of them are included in the observation with the maximum possible five elections. The canton of Zurich further has the largest parliament of all analyzed  cantons, giving it extra influence in the weighted mean analysis. The positive aggregate finding reported in @sec-h1-results therefore remains robust to the exclusion of any single canton.

####  Exploratory Question 1

```{r}
#| label: loco-results-eq1
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: [40, 30, 30]

# Include the original sample as a reference, then omit each canton.
loco_eq1_cases <- c(
  "Full sample",
  sort(setdiff(unique(eq1_points$canton), "GR"))
)

loco_eq1_results <- map_dfr(loco_eq1_cases, function(omitted) {

  eq1_points |>
    filter(canton != "GR", canton != omitted) |>
    group_by(metric, group) |>
    summarise(
      mean_gain_pp = mean(mean_gain_pp),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = group,
      values_from = mean_gain_pp
    ) |>
    mutate(
      omitted_canton = omitted,
      difference_pp = `Below mean` - `At/above mean`
    ) |>
    select(omitted_canton, metric, difference_pp)
})

# Display the two comparisons side by side.
loco_eq1_table <- loco_eq1_results |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = metric,
    values_from = difference_pp
  )

knitr::kable(
  loco_highlight_influence(
    loco_eq1_table, setdiff(names(loco_eq1_table), "omitted_canton")
  ),
  format = "pipe",
  align = c("l", "r", "r"),
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Canton omitted", "Mean size", "Share below 9"
  ),
  caption = paste(
    "Leave-one-canton-out sensitivity of district-characteristic",
    "group differences (percentage points; original cutoffs retained)."
  )
)
```

Omitting Schaffhausen produces the largest absolute change in both comparisons. The difference for mean district magnitude remains negative, whereas the difference for the share of districts below nine seats changes from negative to positive. The direction of the latter comparison therefore depends on Schaffhausen’s inclusion. These robustness checks demonstrate sensitivity to the sample composition.

#### Exploratory Question 2 

```{r}
#| label: loco-results-eq2
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: [22, 26, 26, 26]

loco_eq2_cases <- c(
  "Full sample", # Reference result before excluding any canton.
  sort(setdiff(unique(eq2_elections$canton), "GR"))
)

loco_eq2_results <- map_dfr(loco_eq2_cases, function(omitted) {

  omitted_groups <- eq2_elections |>
    filter(canton == omitted) |>
    pull(quorum) |>
    as.character()

  eq2_elections |>
    filter(canton != "GR", canton != omitted) |> # Remove the whole canton.
    group_by(quorum) |>
    summarise(
      mean_gain_pp = mean(seat_gain_pp), # Equal weight per election.
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = quorum,
      values_from = mean_gain_pp
    ) |>
    mutate(
      omitted_canton = omitted,
      difference_pp = `Without explicit quorum` -
                      `With explicit quorum`,
      # Hide unaffected means after calculating the comparison with that group.
      across(
        all_of(c("Without explicit quorum", "With explicit quorum")),
        ~ if (omitted != "Full sample" && !(cur_column() %in% omitted_groups)) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          .x
        }
      )
    ) |>
    select(
      omitted_canton,
      `Without explicit quorum`,
      `With explicit quorum`,
      difference_pp
    )
})

knitr::kable(
  loco_highlight_influence(
    loco_eq2_results,
    c("Without explicit quorum", "With explicit quorum", "difference_pp")
  ),
  format = "pipe",
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"),
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Canton omitted", "Without quorum (pp)",
    "With quorum (pp)", "Difference (pp)"
  ),
  caption = paste(
    "Leave-one-canton-out sensitivity of the electoral-quorum",
    "comparison. NA marks a group in which the omitted canton has no elections.",
    "Aargau contributes to both groups and is omitted from both.",
    "Difference: without minus with quorum, using the full-sample mean for an unaffected group."
  )
)
```

As in the prior robustness checks the cantons of Zurich and Schaffhausen are responsible for the highest absolute differences. The omission of Schaffhausen reverses the group difference. This means that without the Schaffhausen elections, the average seat-gain share is higher for elections with quorums compared to the ones without quorums. The sample for the without quorum group consists of twelve elections, from which five are from Schaffhausen. Further all Schaffhausen elections, experience an above average seat-share gain. Thus is the observed difference sensitive to Schaffhausen's inclusion and should not be interpreted as a stable relationship between an explicit electoral quroum and the smaller party seat-share gains.

#### Exploratory Question 3
```{r}
#| label: loco-eq3-data
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: [21,21,16,21,21]

loco_eq3_cases <- c(
  "Full sample", # Baseline: omit no additional canton.
  sort(setdiff(unique(eq3_elections$canton), "GR"))
)

loco_eq3_results <- map_dfr(loco_eq3_cases, function(omitted) {

  eq3_elections |>
    filter(canton != "GR", canton != omitted) |>
    arrange(canton, election_number) |>
    group_by(canton) |>
    mutate(
      change_pp = seat_gain_pp - lag(seat_gain_pp) # Within-canton change.
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>
    group_by(election_number) |>
    summarise(
      cantons = n_distinct(canton), # Remaining elections
      mean_gain_pp = mean(seat_gain_pp),
      mean_change_pp = if (all(is.na(change_pp))) {
        NA_real_ # No preceding election for election 1.
      } else {
        mean(change_pp, na.rm = TRUE)
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    filter(
      omitted == "Full sample" |
        election_number %in% eq3_elections$election_number[
          eq3_elections$canton == omitted
        ] # Omit only relevant cantons for each election number
    ) |>
    mutate(omitted_canton = omitted) |>
    select(
      omitted_canton, election_number, cantons,
      mean_gain_pp, mean_change_pp
    )
}) |>
  arrange(election_number, omitted_canton != "Full sample", omitted_canton) |>
  select(election_number, omitted_canton, cantons, mean_gain_pp, mean_change_pp)

# Locate reference rows dynamically because election-number groups vary in size.
loco_eq3_full_sample_rows <- which(loco_eq3_results$omitted_canton == "Full sample")
knitr::asis_output(paste0(
  "```{=typst}\n#[\n#set table(\n",
  "  fill: (x, y) => if y in (",
  paste(loco_eq3_full_sample_rows, collapse = ", "),
  ") { rgb(\"#f2f2f2\") } else { none },\n",
  ")\n```\n"
))
```

```{r}
#| label: loco-results-eq3
#| echo: false
#| tbl-colwidths: [16, 22, 16, 23, 23]

knitr::kable(
  loco_highlight_influence(
    loco_eq3_results, c("mean_gain_pp", "mean_change_pp"),
    groups = "election_number"
  ),
  format = "pipe",
  digits = 2,
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r"),
  col.names = c(
    "Election number", "Canton omitted", "Cantons",
    "Mean gain (pp)", "Mean change (pp)"
  ),
  caption = paste(
    "Leave-one-canton-out sensitivity of successive-election summaries.",
    "Changes are calculated within cantons before averaging.",
    "Only cantons observed at the respective election number are omitted.",
    "The full-sample reference row for each election number is shaded light grey."
  )
)
```

```{=typst}
]
```
For exploratory question three, the robustness check was done for each election number separately. Zurich or Schaffhausen produces the largest absolute change in six out of nine comparisons. The mean seat-share gains remain positive under every omission. However, the mean change from election three to four switches from negative to positive when Zurich is excluded, while the change from election four to five switches from positive to negative when Aargau is excluded. These later transitions include only five respectively three cantons. This makes their averages particularly sensitive to individual cantons.
